admin_cf_setup_s1_text: In the Cloudflare dashboard, open My Profile, then API Tokens, Create Token, Custom token. Add exactly one permission. Nothing can write:
admin_cf_setup_s1_zone: Then set Zone Resources to include your custom domain's zone, or the query returns nothing.
admin_cf_setup_s2_title: Store the token, account id and zone id as secrets
admin_cf_setup_s2_ci: Fastest path — store all three as GitHub repository secrets. From the fork's directory (so gh reads the repo from your origin remote), run:
admin_cf_setup_s2_ci_post_a: gh prompts for each value, so nothing lands in your shell history, and the deploy workflow re-applies repo secrets right before every deploy — so your next deploy picks them up with nothing to remember. No gh? Add them in the GitHub UI under
admin_cf_setup_s2_text: Prefer to set them by hand? None of these touch the database — store them as Pages secrets, then redeploy:
admin_cf_setup_s3_text: Cloudflare Pages binds secrets at deploy time. The GitHub Actions path redeploys for you; if you set the secrets by hand, redeploy now. The edge panel then appears next to your in-app metrics — it reads zone analytics, so your custom domain must be connected (a bare pages.dev URL has no zone data).
admin_cf_setup_callout: Give the token Zone → Analytics: Read and nothing else, so a leaked token can't change anything. It only ever reads your own zone's numbers, so it never becomes the boundary between two forks.
admin_cf_setup_unlocks: a Cloudflare edge panel: cached versus origin requests, total bandwidth, threats blocked. Disconnect anytime by deleting the secret; nothing else on this page depends on it.

admin_vr_guide_link: How to export a VRM from VRChat
admin_vr_guide_title: Export your VRChat avatar as a VRM
admin_vr_guide_lede: The 3D viewer loads a .vrm file. VRChat won't give you one, but if you have the Unity project your avatar was built in, you can export one yourself. This page walks through it end to end.
admin_vr_guide_callout_no_download: You can't download your uploaded VRChat avatar. Once it's on VRChat's servers it's a platform bundle with no way back out. The export starts from your own Unity project.
admin_vr_guide_before_intro: You need three things. Blender isn't one of them, and there's no modeling or code involved.
admin_vr_guide_before_project: **The Unity project your avatar lives in.** If you bought a base and set it up yourself, this is what you have; your materials and textures are already assigned.
admin_vr_guide_before_unity: **Unity 2022.3 LTS.** VRChat pins 2022.3.22f1 and UniVRM needs 2022.3 or later, so the two agree.
admin_vr_guide_before_univrm: **UniVRM** (free). Download the .unitypackage from [the UniVRM releases page on GitHub](https://github.com/vrm-c/UniVRM/releases) — each release ships several artifacts, and you want the plain `UniVRM-….unitypackage`. This guide was verified with v0.131.2.
admin_vr_guide_wont_work: What won't work: an FBX without its textures embedded (it renders untextured grey), and a .glb exported from another platform (it carries that platform's materials, not yours).
admin_vr_guide_step1_title: Work in a copy of your project
admin_vr_guide_step1_body: Don't install UniVRM into your working VRChat project. UniVRM and the VRChat SDK have a history of assembly and shader conflicts, and a broken project can cost you a working avatar setup. Duplicate the project folder first: copy `Assets`, `Packages`, and `ProjectSettings`. Skip `Library`; Unity rebuilds it on first open, which takes a few minutes. Everything from here happens in the copy.
admin_vr_guide_step2_body: `Assets → Import Package → Custom Package`, pick the UniVRM file, import everything. Unity compiles for a while. When it finishes, a **VRM0** entry appears in the menu bar; that's how you know it took. UniVRM lands in `Packages`, not `Assets`, so don't judge the import by browsing the Assets folder — the menu is the reliable check. No menu means the import failed (see troubleshooting below).
admin_vr_guide_step3_title: Make a VRM-safe copy of the avatar
admin_vr_guide_step3_p1: In the scene, duplicate your avatar and work on the duplicate. Remove the VRChat components: avatar descriptor, pipeline manager, PhysBones and their colliders, VRCFury, contacts. The mesh, skeleton, and materials stay.
admin_vr_guide_step3_p2: Decide how the avatar should look before you export. VRM has no radial menu, so toggles, outfit switches, and PhysBone motion don't survive. Whatever is visible in the scene is what you get: set the hood, accessories, and outfit now.
admin_vr_guide_step4_p1: This is the step that makes the file fit. A VRChat avatar carries hundreds of blendshapes for dances, face tracking, and body sliders, and every one stores three deltas per vertex. The viewer shows a static model and uses none of them.
admin_vr_guide_step4_options: The export wizard's **ExportSettings** tab has the controls for this: `ReduceBlendshape` removes the shapes no expression uses, `UseSparseAccessor` stores what's left more compactly, and `OnlyBlendshapePosition` drops each shape's normal and tangent deltas.
admin_vr_guide_step4_p2: Your textures are probably fine as they are. The 7.28 MB above came from removing every blendshape — keep your expressions and the file lands larger, but still comfortably inside the {max} limit at full 2048² resolution.
admin_vr_guide_step5_p1: Poiyomi doesn't exist outside VRChat; a VRM still using it renders wrong or not at all. Switch each material to the `VRM/MToon` shader UniVRM installed and re-assign the base color texture; the slot doesn't always carry over when you change shaders.
admin_vr_guide_step5_p2: **Match each material's cull mode to the original** instead of setting one value for the whole model. Turning culling off everywhere looks harmless, but it can make eyes render blank white: the inside of the eyeball draws over the iris.
admin_vr_guide_step5_p3: Expect close, not identical. Base colors carry over; rim light, outlines, and shadows won't match Unity pixel for pixel. MToon ignores most extra maps (metallic, masks, color shift), and leaving them off is correct.
admin_vr_guide_step6_p1: Select the cleaned avatar and use the export option in the **VRM0** menu. Fill in the title, author, and license fields honestly; they're embedded in the file and travel with it, which makes them the right place to record your base's terms.
admin_vr_guide_step6_p2: Then come back to the upload form: attach the .vrm, fill in credits and license, and pick a poster.
admin_vr_guide_license_callout: The download toggle hides a button; it doesn't prevent access. A browser has to fetch the model bytes to render them, so publishing with the viewer is distribution.
admin_vr_guide_license_p1: If the avatar is on a paid base, the model file isn't yours to redistribute. Most base licenses allow personal use and VRChat uploads and say nothing about hosting the file on your own site, and silence isn't permission.
admin_vr_guide_license_p2: Two clean ways through: ask the base creator (most answer quickly, and a yes in writing settles it), or showcase with clips and renders instead, which raises no redistribution question at all. If you made the model yourself, none of this applies.
admin_vr_guide_trouble_grey_q: The model renders grey and untextured
admin_vr_guide_trouble_grey_a: Usually an FBX uploaded without embedded textures; export a .vrm instead. If a VRM still shows grey, a material lost its base color texture in the MToon switch. Check every slot.
admin_vr_guide_trouble_eyes_a: Cull mode. Set each MToon material's cull value to match the original material instead of disabling culling everywhere; with culling off, the eyeball's inner surface draws over the iris. It looks like a missing texture, but the texture is fine.
admin_vr_guide_trouble_colors_q: The colors are wrong or flat
admin_vr_guide_trouble_colors_a: A Poiyomi material slipped through. Check every material slot on every renderer; some meshes have several. Flatter shading than in-game is normal for MToon and not a fault.
admin_vr_guide_trouble_size_a: Blendshapes, almost always. Strip them (step 4). Textures at 2048² were never the problem.
admin_vr_guide_trouble_proxy_q: The exporter says VRMBlendShapeProxy is required
admin_vr_guide_trouble_proxy_a: ReduceBlendshape leans on VRM expression data a freshly converted VRChat avatar doesn't have yet. Export once without the option, reimport the resulting VRM (that sets up the proxy and its clips), then export again with it on.
admin_vr_guide_trouble_menu_q: There's no VRM menu in Unity
admin_vr_guide_trouble_menu_a: UniVRM didn't import, or compile errors stopped it. Check the console, confirm Unity 2022.3 or later, and re-import with everything selected. Assembly conflicts usually mean you're in your real VRChat project instead of the copy.
admin_vr_guide_trouble_pose_q: The pose is wrong or limbs are twisted
admin_vr_guide_trouble_pose_a: An animation preview or test animator was overriding the pose at export time. Export from a clean, unposed state.
admin_vr_guide_trouble_missing_q: Something is missing or toggled wrong
admin_vr_guide_trouble_missing_a: Toggles don't survive; the scene state at export is what ships. Set the avatar up the way you want it seen and export again.
